record.one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects and teams, with a REST API and an official MCP server.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for apps acting on behalf of users. Personal access tokens (PAT) generated in the developer console. The MCP server uses OAuth only.
record.access_notes: PAT and OAuth app creation are self-serve in the developer console; the quick start says to create a PAT via the developer console with no paid-plan requirement stated. Plan-tier requirement not explicitly confirmed on a pricing page (Asana has a free tier), hence medium confidence. critic: access self_serve_free confirmed; app review is not needed to obtain a token.
record.api_notes: RESTful API at app.asana.com/api/1.0; quick start describes a comprehensive reference for objects, schemas and endpoints. critic: breadth moderate -> broad based on that description (not graded).
record.blocker_notes: critic: app review is only needed to distribute to workspaces beyond your own organization or to list in the app directory; internal/testing use needs no review, so verdict stays ready.

evidence.quote: Asana supports the authorization code grant flow
A personal access token (PAT) contains your security credentials for the Asana platform.
To quickly authorize your API requests, create a personal access token via the developer console
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization.
Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token.
If you're building an internal tool or testing your integration, you can create and use an OAuth app without submitting it for review.
